body: Azure offers three main compute types. Virtual machines run virtualized servers as IaaS, and you control the operating system and software. Containers are lightweight, and unlike VMs you do not manage an operating system for each one. Azure Container Instances is a simple PaaS way to run a container, while Azure Kubernetes Service orchestrates containers. Azure Functions is event-driven and serverless, so it only uses CPU time while it runs, and it scales automatically with demand.
author: claude

body: Azure Virtual Machines run virtualized servers as IaaS. Virtual Machine Scale Sets manage groups of identical, load-balanced VMs that scale out or in automatically, on demand or on a schedule. Availability sets improve resiliency inside a region: VMs are spread across fault domains, which share a possible power or network failure point, and update domains, which reboot together during planned maintenance. Azure Virtual Desktop is a managed service that lets users securely reach Windows desktops and apps hosted in Azure from many devices.
author: claude

body: When you create an Azure virtual machine, you choose three kinds of resources. Compute is the VM size, which sets the number of processor cores and the amount of RAM. Storage is the disks, such as hard disk drives or solid state drives. Networking covers the virtual network, a public IP address and the port configuration. As an IaaS service, you still manage patching, updates and configuration inside the VM, even though Azure provides the hardware.
author: claude

body: Azure gives three main ways to host an application. Virtual machines give you maximum control of the hosting environment and let you configure it exactly as you want. Containers can isolate and manage different parts of the hosting solution individually. Azure App Service is a platform option for building and hosting web apps, background jobs, mobile back ends and REST APIs in the language you choose, without managing infrastructure, and it scales automatically.
author: claude

body: Azure virtual networks let resources such as VMs, web apps and databases communicate with each other, with the internet and with on-premises computers. A virtual network has an isolated address space that is not internet routable, which you can divide into subnets. Peering connects two virtual networks directly, even across regions, and the traffic stays on the Microsoft backbone and never enters the public internet. Azure DNS hosts DNS domains and provides name resolution using Azure infrastructure.
author: claude

body: To connect on-premises networks to Azure there are two options. Azure VPN Gateway sends encrypted traffic through a private tunnel across the public internet. It supports site-to-site connections for datacenters, point-to-site connections for single devices, and network-to-network connections. Azure ExpressRoute is a private connection through a connectivity provider that does not go over the public internet, which gives more reliability, faster speeds, consistent latency and higher security than typical internet connections.
author: claude

body: An endpoint is how a resource is reached on the network. A public endpoint has a public IP address and can be accessed from anywhere in the world. A private endpoint exists inside a virtual network and has a private IP address from that network's address space. Azure virtual networking supports both, to allow communication between external or internal resources and internal resources. Service endpoints can link resources such as Azure SQL databases and storage accounts to virtual networks.
author: claude
